response.rationale: Yes, A and B appear to be the same concept: the treatment product (a veterinary product with a withdrawal period). In A, TreatmentService (node 2912145e8ad12343, src/business/treatmentService.ts) creates a product with `this.products.create({ name: requireText(name, "name"), withdrawalDays })`. The graph shows this call goes to ProductRepository.create, and ProductRepository is injected into TreatmentService through its constructor. In B, ProductRepository (node f86df271c26e9cd6, src/persistence/repositories.ts) stores these same entities in `private readonly items = new Map<string, ProductRecord>();`. So 'Treatment Product' in the business layer and 'Product' in the persistence layer look like one thing under two names. I can't see the ProductRecord definition, so this rests on the call link and the withdrawalDays field.
